name: West !Xoon
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Guldemann, Tom and Christfried Naumann 2015. Grammatical relations in the West !Xoon dialect of Taa; no open online copy found.

sources.note: Reports Traill's four tones for East !Xoon and 'two tones (DoBeS 2008 on West !Xoon)'; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: DoBeS Taa documentation project (Güldemann, Kießling, Naumann, Boden). 'Language' page of the Taa project site, last update 2017.
sources.note: First-hand project summary of West !Xoon phonology: consonant chart (88 consonants under cluster analysis, from Naumann 2016), lexical stems C(C)V(C)V / C(C)VN, two noun tone classes; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Boden, Gertrud. 2005. Western versus Eastern !Xoon: differences, politics, and documentation. Language Archives Newsletter 7: 2-7.
sources.note: Ethnographic/political DoBeS project report on the West-East !Xoon split; no phonology; 'stress' occurs only as an English verb (p. 4).

sources.citation: Downing, Laura J. 2004. What African languages tell us about accent typology. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 37: 101-136 (Sec. 4, pp. 111-112).
sources.note: p. 111: 'All the Khoisan languages are described as having tone, and I could find no discussion of stress in the existing Khoisan literature'; infers foot-initial strength in !Xóõ from Traill 1985's consonant distribution. Second-hand, on East !Xoon, not West !Xoon.

sources.citation: Traill, Anthony. 1994. A !Xóõ Dictionary (QKF 9). Köln: Köppe. (archive.org scanned text layer, held under huaa1248)
sources.note: East !Xoon (Botswana), not West !Xoon. Full-text grep: 'stress' only as English verb/gloss, 'prominence' only of a labial offglide; four lexical tones on the bimoraic stem; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: DoBeS Taa project (Güldemann, Kießling, Naumann, Boden). c. 2009-2017. Taa (West !Xoon) sketch grammar, deposited in the DoBeS Taa corpus, The Language Archive (MPI Nijmegen).

sources.note: The project page states the corpus contains a sketch grammar of Taa; the phonology chapter of a DoBeS sketch would be the first-hand West !Xoon description most likely to state stress facts.

sources.citation: Naumann, Christfried. 2016. The phoneme inventory of Taa (West !Xoon dialect). In Rainer Vossen & Wilfrid H. G. Haacke (eds.), Lone Tree: Scholarship in the Service of the Koon: Essays in Memory of Anthony T. Traill, 311-351. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonological description of West !Xoon (41 pp., Glottolog hhtype phonology); most likely place for a statement on stress/prominence or an explicit 'tone, no stress' remark.

sources.citation: Güldemann, Tom & Christfried Naumann. 2015. Grammatical relations in the West !Xoon dialect of Taa. 14 pp. Paper presented at the IAAW African linguistics research colloquium, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin.
